subject: electrical-computer
audience: FE Electrical and Computer candidates and engineering students
title: The Four-Channel FDM Link That Needed 95 kHz
featured_title: THE FOUR-CHANNEL FDM LINK THAT NEEDED 95 KHZ

presentation.challenge: Four 20 kHz channels looked like an 80 kHz job—until the guard bands were counted.

practice.primary_question: How do guard bands change the total spectrum required by a frequency-division multiplexed system?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Adding only the channel bandwidths and forgetting the guard bands required between adjacent FDM channels.

case_dna.target_misconception: Four 20 kHz FDM channels always fit inside exactly 80 kHz of spectrum.
case_dna.why_plausible: Summing channel bandwidths is the obvious first calculation and is correct only when no spacing is required.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: Four adjacent channels have three internal boundaries. With a 5 kHz guard band between neighbors, total span is 4×20+3×5=95 kHz.
case_dna.corrected_model: For N equal FDM channels with guard band G only between adjacent channels, total occupied span is N B + (N-1) G.

problem_statement: A frequency-division multiplexing plan combines four channels, each occupying 20 kHz, with a required 5 kHz guard band between adjacent channels. The planner reserves 80 kHz by summing only the channel bandwidths, but the fourth channel cannot fit without violating spacing. Calculate the required spectrum and identify the correct number of guard bands.
fixed_constraints: Guard band = 5 kHz between adjacent channels
No outer-edge guard bands are required in this exercise

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The channels totaled 80 kHz. The spectrum plan still overflowed.
facts: Guard band between adjacent channels: 5 kHz
gates.prompt: How many internal guard bands are needed between four adjacent channels?

gates.label: Theory
gates.heading: Choose the correct FDM span model

options.label: Use N channel bandwidths plus N-1 internal guard bands
options.reason: Four adjacent channels create three gaps between neighboring channels.

options.label: Use only 4×20 kHz because guard bands do not consume spectrum
options.reason: Guard bands occupy frequency space even though they do not carry the intended channel information.

options.label: Use four guard bands between four channels
options.reason: There are only three internal boundaries between four adjacent channels when no outer guards are specified.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the required spectrum
gates.prompt: For four 20 kHz channels and three 5 kHz internal guard bands, what total span (kHz) is required?

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Lay out the four channels
gates.result: The four-channel FDM allocation requires 95 kHz.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the FDM bandwidth
gates.prompt: Calculate 4×20 kHz + 3×5 kHz. Enter the total required span.
gates.success: 80 kHz of channel bandwidth plus 15 kHz of guard bands gives 95 kHz.
gates.hint: Four channels have three spaces between adjacent channels.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: The spectrum layout shows the missing 15 kHz

cards.text: Four adjacent channels create three internal gaps.
Three 5 kHz guard bands add 15 kHz, giving 95 kHz total.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the spectrum plan
report: C1. There are four 20 kHz channels.
C2. Adjacent channels require 5 kHz guard bands.
C3. Therefore 80 kHz of spectrum is sufficient.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It omits the three internal guard bands.

evidence_choices.label: 4×20 + 3×5 = 95 kHz
evidence_choices.reason: This includes both channel bandwidth and internal guard-band spacing.

correction.template: The required FDM spectrum is {span} kHz when the three internal guard bands are included.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Fit the system into a 90 kHz allocation
gates.constraint: Keep four channels and 5 kHz internal guard bands.

options.label: Reduce each channel bandwidth to at most 18.75 kHz
Keep each channel at 20 kHz because 4×20=80 kHz
options.reason: That still ignores the 15 kHz of guard bands.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply the FDM guard-band rule
gates.prompt: Three 10 kHz channels use 2 kHz guard bands between adjacent channels. What total span is required?

options.label: 36 kHz
options.reason: That counts three internal guard bands instead of two.

gates.explanation: With guard bands only between adjacent channels, N channels have N-1 internal guard bands.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the multiplexing plan
gates.confirmation: I confirm that FDM spectrum planning must include the bandwidth occupied by required guard bands.

items.label: What failed
items.value: An 80 kHz allocation was too small for the four-channel plan.

items.label: What was assumed
items.value: Guard bands were treated as if they consumed no spectrum.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Total span = NB + (N-1)G when guard bands occur only between adjacent channels.

seo.seo_title: FDM Bandwidth With Guard Bands: Why 80 kHz Becomes 95 kHz | FE E-037
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Case E-037: four 20 kHz FDM channels with 5 kHz guard bands require 95 kHz of spectrum, not 80 kHz.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FDM bandwidth guard bands FE exam
seo.excerpt: FDM channel bandwidths are not the whole spectrum plan. Guard bands between channels also consume frequency space.
seo.direct_answer: For four 20 kHz FDM channels with 5 kHz guard bands only between adjacent channels, there are three guard bands. Total spectrum is 4×20 + 3×5 = 95 kHz.

faqs.q: How many internal guard bands are there between four FDM channels?
faqs.a: Three, assuming guard bands are required only between adjacent channels.

faqs.q: What total span is needed for four 20 kHz channels with 5 kHz guard bands?
